utterances.text: This was at the time when the check-points were only being erected and at the time when the military vehicles were able to go out of the barracks to Borovo Selo and Erdut to get the necessary supplies, and in such cases when these vehicles would pass along those villages, civilians would ask them to be transported back to the barracks, under the tarpaulin of the military vehicle because they wanted to seek shelter there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What became of the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: When it was on its way to Borovo Selo, it was hit by hand-held rocket launcher. The officer and the soldiers were killed on the spot and the vehicle was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Speaking of the barracks, you mentioned something about the barracks being surrounded by houses. Does that mean that houses belonging to civilians, Vukovar's residents, were right there next to the barracks? Was this only in one side of the barracks or all?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: That's on three sides of the barracks. The fourth side was booby trapped by them. There was no mine field there and they could retreat, but they came under fire from the flanks by snipers and there was mortar fire all the time raining on the buildings and the barracks facilities. When I entered the barracks, all the shrubbery and the plants there were gone. All you could see all around the barracks courtyard were craters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You talk about sniper fire, about shooting. You're talking about the houses around the barracks and those were positions held by the other side?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, the ZNG and the MUP. When we reached the Mitrovica Brigade, when we left Petrova Gora, it was then I found out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. We'll get to that. Just another question about the barracks. What you just described at one point in time the barracks was entirely besieged on all sides, you couldn't get in or out and it was under permanent fire. Is that what you were trying to say, sir?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, no running water, no food and a number of wounded inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You were with your unit at Petrova Gora at the time, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you please just not speak at the same time as me, so that we have answers and questions in a consecutive fashion. You said you headed for Petrova Gora. Does that mean that your unit went on a mission to do with the barracks and how distant was this from the area in which you were?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Perhaps 700 to 800 metres as the crow flies, up to a kilometre. We were surrounded as well. We had Pater behind us but we didn't know that that too was surrounded. There was a lot of uncertainty. The barracks had been under siege for days and we were left without running water and electricity. Our supplies had been cut off too. We were under constant mortar fire. We had to bury Galovic's father out in the garden. We couldn't reach any of the town's cemeteries and we had to bury our wounded in our own back and front yards. We were under fire throughout and so was the barracks. We wanted to cross Atar to reach Negoslavci in an attempt to break out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: At one point in time you decided to try to get to Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Precisely, to see what we could do about the barracks and the soldiers there, the manpower at Petrova Gora as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: This road that you took is the road to the barracks also?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: No. That's in the opposite direction from the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you please indicate that on the map, the same map that you were looking at a while ago. If I could have assistance please for Exhibit 156 to be brought up again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: It's right here, it's between Petrova Gora and Solidarnost street. There is a road through Dola and we reached Atar down this road. There was a field here, a corn field, and we saw soldiers stationed between Petrovci and Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Would you please use an arrow to mark a direction and put a number 1 there, please?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: This is the road -- I sent a security platoon through the corn field to position themselves there to keep us from falling into an ambush. As soon as we reached the clearing with our vehicles we saw soldiers there. We had a Yugoslav flag with us and we moved in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can we actually see that on the map, this area?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: No. The road to Petrovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you please show the continuation of this road to Petrovci?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Can we please scroll up slightly?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could use a bigger map and then you could mark these points for us again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have a bigger map, please? Or rather, can we zoom out and look at the entire area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is Velepromet. It's covering the area I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You can use an arrow to write over that, please. Perhaps now you can see it.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: This is excellent. I can see everything here. There was the direction, and the soldiers were here where it says Petrovacka Dola. There is the tip there, and a mound of sorts. That's where the soldiers were and we noticed them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Where the arrow is, could you put a number 1 there again. And could you please put a circle around the area in which you met those JNA units and put a number 2 there, sir, please?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What happened now? You met these JNA soldiers.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: We displayed a Yugoslav flag and the soldiers thought it was Croats advancing and they nearly fired on us from a tank. At the last minute they realised who we were. We approached them. We told them about the situation and we went to the command in Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we move on, I don't think we will be needing this map for the time being for you to mark anything. And I move that the newly made markings be admitted into evidence, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 769.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Mr. Jaksic, let's move on. You say that after coming across these JNA units -- we don't need the map any more. You say you went to Negoslavci, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Where to in Negoslavci? Who did you see?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I reported to the command of the Mitrovica Brigade and I went to see the then Lieutenant Colonel Ilija Jokic. When I told him about the situation, he had a map there and the map said no Serbs in Vukovar. When I told him about the situation, what we still were holding on to and how we had organised ourselves, he gave me a radio to get in touch with the barracks. I knew all of the officers there. And my brother was there too. So I decided to move up one level or to step up a gear and to go for liberating the barracks and not just relieving the siege.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you went to see Lieutenant Colonel Jokic, how did you introduce yourself?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Jokic had reserve captain Marko Draguljac right next to him. He was a reserve officer in his brigade. He saw me coming, through the window. They told him and he explained who I was and what I was doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. But at the time you were commander of this territorial unit. Did you clearly state that to Jokic and everybody else there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Which demands did you make on the army?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: When I found out that there were some wounded in the barracks and that they had gone off to evacuate them, the first tank driving down that road towards the barracks was hit by an arm-breast rocket from a ZNG check-point, killing the entire crew. When the tank was destroyed, they started out through the field trying to reach the barracks but the next tank drove straight into a minefield. The crew managed to get away but they captured the tank and its weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What do you mean its weapons?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: There was an anti-aircraft machine-gun. They seized this and they used it to fire at Petrova Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Just briefly, which period of time are we looking at?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: That's prior to the 14th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You say this was prior to the 14th of September. You're talking about this attempt to get closer to the barracks, right, the JNA attempt?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. And my arrival. I arrived up to a fortnight before the 14th of September, to see Jokic, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So your arrival and this attempted break-through, that was in early September, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say this thing with the barracks was before the 14th of September, how long before was this attempt by the JNA tanks to approach the barracks?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What then became of you or your unit? Did you go straight back to Petrova Gora? What happened next?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I went over to the Novi Sad corps with Ilija Kojic. I asked General Bratic, I pleaded with him. I told him about the situation on the ground and the situation of the barracks, and I pleaded with him to try to lift the siege of the barracks and try to evacuate the soldiers who were stuck inside the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You say you went to see Ilija Kojic. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Ilija Kojic was Vule Sasochin's replacement in Borovo Selo. He was the commander of Borovo Selo's defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: But you met up with him in Novi Sad, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So what was the result of your talks with General Bratic? Did anything happen?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: He lent me his ear. I explained to him what the situation was and then he sent me to see Ilija Jokic or Kojic saying that everything would be okay and that soon forces would be sent in to evacuate the soldiers who were stuck in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Page 51, line 4, it says he sent me to see Ilija Jokic or Kojic. Let's clarify this. Was it Ilija Jokic or Ilija Kojic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Ilija Jokic, the commander of the Mitrivica brigade, his command was stationed in the village of Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. From this point on, what about the road to Petrova Gora? Was it free or not?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. I got a radio from commander Jokic. We got some vehicles and some infantry weapons. I drove back down the same road to Petrova Gora, awaiting a signal for an attack on the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do I understand you correctly, the deal was for you to go back to Petrova Gora and to await the commencement of an attack, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. My task was to organise some men. As soon as I received a signal, I was to switch on my radio and I was to be off to Svetozar Markovica, cross the barricade, join up with the tanks and go down a street to Vuteks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Fine. Where were we? You've heard the interpreters. They want you to speak a bit more slowly. So if you could please give us this entire answer all over again?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: You mean my task was to and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: To organise an assault group to attack the barricade at Svetozara Markovica street, to crush it. To join up with the tanks along the Petrovci road at the far end of Svetozara Markovica street.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: It's a bit imprecise. Did you have tanks or you were supposed to join up with tanks?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: We were supposed to join up with the tanks of the Mitrovica Brigade, the active forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was this plan carried out and when, if so?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was carried out on the 14th of September. We, the infantry, were supposed to watch out for the tanks and they were supposed to provide us with support so that we could move on the barracks and the town in order to lift the siege.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you please use the map to show how exactly you advanced on the barracks and the roads which you took. If we could please have that exhibit. And I hope this is the very last time, Exhibit 156. Perhaps if we could blow this up slightly, we need the area between Petrova Gora and the JNA barracks. The middle portion of the map. This is fine. Thank you. Will you please indicate the road out of Petrova Gora which you took?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: This is where their check-point was and we went along this road, and cleared the area, joined up with the tanks there, and then went along the Proleterska street towards Vuteks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Pause there a bit. Can you please mark with number 1 the first section of your movement where you lifted the blockade and -- and can you show us where this was?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And please indicate the point where you met up with the tanks of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Right away. This is number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And where was this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: That was the junction of Svetozara Markovica and Proleterska street.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And then you moved back along a different route?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. The adjacent -- along the adjacent street. Should I mark it with number 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. At the far end of it, on the top -- at the top of the arrow.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What was the further direction of your movement?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: We had to protect the flank of the army and there was the Territorial Defence Battalion from Negoslavci that was moving in toward the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Would you please indicate with a line the movement toward the barracks of both the infantry moving from Negoslavci --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: We have the movement along the road from Negoslavci to the barracks. This was their line of movement. Should I mark it with number 4?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall when this event took place?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: On the 14th of September 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you reach the JNA barracks on that day?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does that include the other units as well?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Please explain.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: On that day, when we launched the attack in Proleterska street there was a large train carriage on the railroad track that runs along the road and it was mined. We were unable to pass through. It was under tank fire but it wasn't very helpful. We did not think it helpful either to activate the explosives because we would simply cause the carriage to roll over. As it was already late in the afternoon, I decided that we should spend the night at that point reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can I stop you there. I don't think we will need the map any longer. We won't be making any markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this map into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 770, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said that you spent the night between the 14th and the 15th of September there. Can you tell us what happened next?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: On that night, I tasked a group to carry out reconnaissance around the railway carriage. There was a very decrepit house there and I asked the tank to pass along and past the house so as to demolish one corner of the house in order to enable the armoured unit that were to follow to pass along it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And did you manage to do that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was near day break that we managed to get past that house in a tank and carry on toward Vuteks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: We reached Vuteks and had almost gone past it. I still had my radio with me, and I heard the members of the ZNG instructing their own lot to let us pass Vuteks where we would come under their mortar fire. The battery of my radio set was already running empty. I lost my contacts with them and this was how it remained until the arrival of the guards brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you please repeat part of your answer as it doesn't seem to have been recorded. You said that Jokic issued an order in reaction to what you were able to hear on the radio.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Jokic issued me with an order and I immediately carried it out. The order was to the effect that I should withdraw from Vuteks and that I should remain at the Radnicka street until further orders of attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And was there in fact another attack launched by you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: No. It was impossible because I simply didn't have enough men. We also had to cover Petrova Gora and our front line had become doubled.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: We went to Sajmiste where we waited for reinforcements in order to advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does it mean that in a way you were moving toward Petrova Gora in order to cover that area too?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was the part of Petrova Gora in the direction of the barracks and Sajmiste. Petrova Gora, Radnicka Conosija up to the barracks was the stretch of the area that was free.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: At that point, as you were holding those positions, what happened to the barracks?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I went over to the barracks. The unit that was there had already been exhausted and left the barracks to take up another position. It was replaced by a unit under the command of Major Mitrov.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did it mean that at that point the barracks was fully liberated and safe?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: No. The barracks was under constant fire from the other side, from the direction of Mitnica. On one occasion, Major Dimitrov said that the situation in the barracks was unbearable, and asked that he be allowed to retreat from the barracks and that later on, when the occasion arose, it would be quite easy to retake it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I just want to point your attention to the fact that initially it was recorded Mitrov as his name in the transcript but you said later on -- and his name in fact is Dimitrov; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Is my understanding correct, you said that you were physically in the barracks. However, the other parts of the town were under the control of the ZNG members; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, it was the Petrova Gora area and the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was it for this reason that Major Dimitrov asked that the units be allowed to retreat?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, because the mortar fire made any movement of the units there impossible, and the life in the barracks was untenable under constant mortar fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go back to Petrova Gora. At that point, it was in touch with the barracks?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, and Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What became of your unit?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: The men who were there at that point still in the town joined the unit at Petrova Gora. We managed to double the line that we held. We organised ourselves according to a military hierarchy. We set up a detachment, an independent TO unit. We organised logistics support. I had a reserve officer Antic whom I appointed to be the commander for logistics. His duty was to provide food supplies, equipment, weapons, and he also had to secure facilities for the men to maintain a certain hygiene level, to take their baths and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, the unit doubled in strength but so did the line that you held?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was it at this point, or perhaps later on, that you reorganised yourselves, established companies and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was just before the 2nd of October that the men at Petrova Gora numbered 344 men, without the logistics staff. I had four companies. The 1st Company had 117 men. The 2nd one, 110. And the third, 72. The fourth had 45 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Tell me, you remained the commander of the entire unit?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you have a deputy?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Ivanovic, Milan was my deputy. He was also a reserve officer and his specialty was engineering.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you appoint commanders of the four companies?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: As I did not have any reserve officers to command over these companies, I chose the men who proved to be capable, decisive and courageous in battle. I picked those out and then left it up to them to decide who was going to be in command of which company.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You stated that there weren't any trained officers you could entrust these duties to, and that therefore you were forced to rely on men who had proved to be good in fighting?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Milorad Vujovic was the commander of the first company. Miroljub rather than Milorad.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Stanko Vujanovic was the commander of the second. Miroslav Pejic commanded the third company. And Sinisa Fot the fourth. The commander of the fourth company was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You're referring to Sinisa Fot?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: At the time, was there a TO staff in the area, and if so, where was it located?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Vukovar did not have a TO staff at the time. Just before the attack on the 14th September, Slobodan Grahovac and Milo Zelac came to Vukovar when I was with Vujic with a view to establishing a TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was there a staff of the TO in Sid?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Slobodan Grahovac was in Sid and that was where the TO staff or headquarters was at the time, tasked with organising men and deploying them to the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, there was no organised Vukovar TO staff at the time?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Please let me finish. There was the staff led by Slobodan Grahovac in Sid and this staff dealt with the calling up of the men and sending them to the front line and I presume that it was mobilising men from that particular area. Would you please clarify the following? As the staff was located in Sid, did it in a way also represent Vukovar and the surrounding areas in terms of mobilising men?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: They only called up men who had fled Vukovar and were now located in Serbia. They wanted to join the Vukovar front line and were organised by that structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was a TO staff organised in Vukovar? If so, when?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: There was an order sometime around mid-October.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: A while ago you spoke about the 2nd of October. What is that in relation to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: On the 1st of October we introduced the Guards Brigade to the front. On the 2nd of October, we moved on with the liberation of Vukovar under the command of the Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was it just the Guards Brigade or other units too? And what was the military term for that area?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: The military term was operations group south. That was south of the Vuka River. All the villages between Mircovci and Tovarnik south of Vukovar, everything was under operations groups south, commanded by Colonel Bajo Bujat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: How long was --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Bajo Bujat stayed for sometime after the 2nd of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Who replaced him?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Colonel Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You spoke of operations group south. Was there such a thing as operations group north?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was north of the south one. It took up the area between the Danube and Tenja and all the fringe villages near Vukovar. The northern sector, north of the Vuka River.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So if we leave the Danube aside, the demarcation line between the areas of responsibility of these two operations groups would be the river Vuka, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So you could say that the bridges over the Vuka were between the two operations groups, south of the Vuka you had operations group south, and north of the river, you had operations group north. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Upon the arrival of the Guards Brigade and its joining the fray, your unit, or at least that's my understanding, continues to fight alongside with them, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you please tell me what happened later, after the 2nd of October, which you say is the day that marks the beginning of your cooperation with the Guards Brigade? Did your unit continue to work with the Guards Brigade and how?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Prior to the 2nd of October, there was the preparation for introducing the Guards Brigade. But I sent out nine scouts for the Guards Brigade assault groups, and then they brought two detachments to the front line. That night, the first thing that was agreed is that to have the Petrova Gora detachment deployed along the front and to try to advance on the river Vuka from there. However, just on the eve of the attack, Mr. Mrksic gave me an order. He said, we are local people. We know the layout, we know the town, we know all the villages, more so than the Guards Brigade. He said we should go as far as Petrova Gora and take the entire line, as far as the left Bara, the water tower, and the whole line should be held by the territorials, in front of the Guards Brigade. That each of the detachments should have several TO members at the front line and that these TO people who had familiarity, a high degree of familiarity with the area should take them around and show them around.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And is that how it was?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You were still a TO commander at the time, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Petrova Gora detachment, commander of the Petrova Gora detachment. That's what I was at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was a TO unit organised for the whole operations group then or later?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Later, when there was a meeting of all the village commanders in operations group south, I found out that I was appointed TO commander of operations group south.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was this tantamount to setting up a staff for the TO operations in group south?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And you were supposed to be in charge of this staff or headquarters, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. However, Colonel Mrksic said, "This is a political post. Let's liberate Vukovar first and then you can take it from there with your politics. First the fighting, first things first. This is not as important right now." That's what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does that mean that exercise in command was more about meeting in the headquarters and spending less time at the front line or something else?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: That's how it was supposed to be. However my deputy Mile Uzelac was the chief of the pre-war TO staff in Vukovar. He was an operative, he loved the job, and he was much better at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you tell us where this headquarters was, the TO staff?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: At Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, you didn't spend that much time there, you spent most of your time at --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I went to maybe two meetings altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Talking about meetings, were you called to any meetings? Did you go to any meetings chaired by Colonel Mrksic at his Negoslavci headquarters with his subordinate officers?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Every day, in the operations room, the briefing, the assignment, every day, at about 1600 hours, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So you were a regular participant in these meetings chaired by Colonel Mrksic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: A while ago we spoke about the TO staff in operations group south. You spoke about this entire area that it covered. In addition to this, was there a Vukovar TO staff or was this the same thing?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: It was the same thing at the time, the same for both. It covered the area under operations group south, all the villages, and then later, when the town of Vukovar was liberated, a special TO staff was set up for Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were there any assistant commanders for the TO staff?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Milo Uzelac was my deputy. There was Lazo Pejic; security, Ilija Vucetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Go slowly with the names, please.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Lazo Pejic, Ilija Vucetic; logistics, Milan Milic; Rukat Sparustakovic; signals, Jovica Kresovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you please repeat Jovica's last name?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Kresovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Something else, Mile Uzelac was your deputy, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And then security and then we can't figure it out.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Ilija Vucetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm about to move on to a different topic now and we are nearing the time for our break, so if Your Honour agrees, I think this might be a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Domazet. And we'll resume at just after 25 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Before we start, Mr. Jaksic, could I just ask you again to answer slowly and make a pause. Sometimes I was compelled to motion to you by hand in order to get you to slow down. So please, for the benefit of the record, please slow down, especially when you get to names. Mr. Jaksic, you spoke about your company commanders and you mentioned Sinisa Fot and you pointed out that he was an ethnic Croat. You said that there were Croats in your unit too. I would like to say something about him. He was a commander. What sort of fighter was he? What became of him? Can you tell us more about that, please?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Sinisa and his brother Darko Fot were pro-Yugoslav. They were at all the anti-HDZ meetings and all the meetings that were in favour of Yugoslavia. They fought for that. They lived in our neighbourhood and that's why they joined us. He was an exceptional fighter. You can only see that sort of fighter in movies like Rambo. So much desire, so much propulsion, so much energy. Why was he like that? Probably because he had been arrested by the ZNG and tortured. They threw him in a prison eventually realising he was a Croat so he was released. But they broke his collar bone in the process. Once he was out of prison, it was probably because of that that he fought so hard. It was probably because of everything they had done to him that he turned against them and that he became such an exceptional fighter for our cause. Above all else, he was a patriot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Is this man still alive?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: No. He was killed. His brother, Darko, was seriously wounded but at least he survived. He now lives and works in Novi Sad for the local customs office.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was Sinisa killed during the fighting in Vukovar or later on?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: During the fighting in Vukovar, on the 2nd of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You were saying that your commanders had no proper military training. Did you mean all these whom you have just listed? You spoke about Vujovic, Vujanovic, Fot and Pejic, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, quite right. Just one thing, if I may. There is a correction to be made. I didn't mean military training. Though all had some military training but they were not officers. They weren't trained to be officers. They had all done their regular military terms, they all knew about warfare. They all knew about the international law of war. As soldiers they knew about all these things. The only thing they weren't trained for was to serve as officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. When you speak about the law of war, during your stint at Bileca, during your training there, were you taught about the Geneva Conventions and all that? Were you familiarised with the substance of the Geneva Conventions?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Certainly. The law of war, the Geneva Conventions, every single soldier had to know about these, and the officers were particularly familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Throughout the operations in Vukovar, you were a TO commander there. Did you have any such orders? Did you personally issue any orders about these conventions and the application of the law of war?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did. Mile Mrksic was adamant and he gave the appropriate orders that all prisoners of war shall be treated in the spirit of the law of war and the Geneva Conventions. All of us subordinates from the operations staff, whenever Mrksic was in command, we always got such orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You speak about these meetings. Which precise meetings do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: The operations staff, whenever we came to briefings and whenever we came to receive orders by the commander of the operations group, and he handed out these orders to everyone alike. Also concerning this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about you personally as the commander of your unit? At the time it was first set up, at the time it grew, did you caution your own soldiers from your own unit about these things?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I most certainly did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: As you explained you became commander of that Petrova Gora TO unit, and then as the operation wore on you became commander of the operations group south TO. What about when the liberation of Vukovar occurred? Were you still occupying that position at the time?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: How come?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: The fighting itself is something that effects the human mind. It's something that affects one's emotions. I was beginning to notice in myself some disquieting signs of an incipient Vietnam syndrome. I was made of iron during the war, facing all the horrors, soldiers, maimed, being brought back from the front line. However, as the operation wore on I began to sense myself reseeding a little. That was towards the very end, very late on, in the fighting. That was when Milovo Brdo had just fallen. Sljivancanin once told Miroljub Vujic when we were at the headquarters, from now on you'll be the commander, once this is over you'll speak on behalf of the staff. When Milovo Brdo fell, I was no longer in that position, I was no longer the commander of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You say the fall of Milovo Brdo, can you specify that in terms of a time line?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I think that was on about the 16th or the 17th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So several days before the fall of Vukovar, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: At the time, or at any time, did you ever receive a written decision on your removal?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you accept this decision? Did you then cease to exercise command? Did you then cease to attend meetings and briefings at Colonel Mrksic's?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I accepted it for what it was and I stopped going to briefings.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: On page 67, line 15 it says, Sljivancanin once told Miroljub Vujic. It's an important matter and it appears that the name is wrong.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Miroljub Vujovic, Vujovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I believe we have got the matter clarified now. It was indeed an error. The person we were talking about Miroljub Vujovic, the commander of the first company; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Once again this man named Vujovic had no background as a military officer; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Line 10, page 68, it says Jovic as the commander of the first company. It's supposed to be Vujovic, Miroljub Vujovic. But I believe the matter is sufficiently clarified. I'd just like to go back to one thing, then. When you stepped down, do you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: That was at the headquarters of the first assault battalion of the Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was there any sort of reaction on your part or did you simply get reconciled with that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I just accepted it for what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you take part in any of the briefings with Captain Mrksic thereafter or?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Well, as I was removed from my position, I withdrew completely from there and did not take part in these activities any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You stated that that was either on the 16th or 17th, in any event, on the eve of the fall of Vukovar, and you stated that you did not attend their meetings any longer. However, at the time the Guards Brigade was still in the area, did you have occasion to see Colonel Mrksic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I saw Colonel Mrksic on the 20th of November after the fall of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And why was this, since you no longer held the position, as you stated?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Representatives of the government arrived and Milos Vojnovic who was a representative of the Court, who took part in the conversation, told me to go to Colonel Mrksic and to plead with him that the war criminals, persons who had committed war crimes, in the area of Vukovar, that they be allowed to stay behind and to stand trial before a local court.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Before I move on, there is this one point that is unclear in the transcript. You said that representatives of the government arrived. First of all, which government do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: The government of the district of Slavonia Baranja and Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Led by who?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: The transcript says representative of a court. I suppose he was the representative of the court of the district?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, Milos Vojnovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Milos Vojnovic used to be a judge before the war, I suppose?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. He graduated from the Belgrade school of law.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was he appointed to be the judge for that district by that incumbent government?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object to that, Your Honour. I object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner. Mr. Domazet, this would appear to be an important matter and you're putting the words directly in the witness's mouth.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it seems to me that in -- on line 13, page 69, it was stated that the representative of the court told the witness to go and see Colonel Mrksic. I asked the witness who the representative of the court was and the witness replied that he was Milos Vojnovic, hence my follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What was the subject of your conversation with Milos Vojnovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: He told me that since we had all the hallmarks of a state, we had the judiciary, the police structure had already been formed by then, we had the health service in place, the schooling system and all the other attendant institutions, in his opinion, there was no need for these people to be tried by other jurisdictions. We had competent judges who were perfectly capable of bringing these proceedings about.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Where did this exchange between you and Vojnovic take place?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: At Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You've told us what he told you. Was there anything else he requested from you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: He asked that all those persons in respect of whom there was suspicion and knowledge that they had committed a crimes, should be isolated and held in custody and brought to trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: As you say on the 20th, you were no longer the commander of the TO. Was he aware of this? Was it precisely because of that that he spoke to you? Was this matter discussed at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You're asking this witness the mental state of another individual. Unless there was some conversation as to positions, this should not be allowed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, we are getting on to an area of some sensitivity, so the only evidence the Chamber will take any notice of is that that comes from the witness, not anything you might say. So you're going to have to get the witness to say what you want, not put critical words to him and then say, "Is that right?" Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I wanted to discuss the matter of the witness's position but I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you tell us what else you talked about and what happened next?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Vojnovic knew that I had been in contact with Mrksic all the time and that I was able to see that through. He didn't have anyone else close at hand to mediate between him and Mrksic. That's why he suggested that I go and do that. I agreed and went to see Mrksic at the headquarters of the Guards Brigade. As entry was not allowed to just anyone into the Guards Brigade premises, Mr. Mrksic did see me because he knew me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Please describe the conversation for us.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I told him what Mr. Vojnovic had asked, that the criminals be allowed to stay in the area and not be forwarded to Serbia. Mrksic's response was that this was out of the question, that all these people would be shipped off to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You say that he was adamant in his position. What specifically are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I was referring to the tone of his voice, which was indicative of the fact that he was adamant and could not be reassured at any cost.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was this where the conversation ended?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: It was very brief. When I received his adamant negative reply, I went back to Vojnovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Where did you meet with Vojnovic for the second time?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Also at Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you recall any particular reaction on the part of Vojnovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: He got reconciled with that. He knew that this was an agreement along the hierarchy. However, Hadzic, who I saw at Velepromet, asked me to take him to Petrova Gora to see the area and to visit the people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were you mentioning Belgrade? Did I hear you well? No, because I can't find that in the transcript. If you haven't mentioned Belgrade, tell us so. If you have, tell us what it was about.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I said that if Colonel Mrksic had received an order then he must have received it from the top, from his superiors in the command, and no one was able to change that order or to have any bearing on it. It could only have been done by the superior to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This is all speculation. I said that if Mrksic had received an order then he must have received it from the top so that's now a double speculation from his superiors in command -- a triple speculation and no one was able to change that order or have any bearing on it which is based on speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is the evidence, Mr. Weiner. It is patently speculative and therefore of no weight. Thank you. Carry on, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. It was not my question that elicited such an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm just pointing out the witness is guessing. And so we -- it's not going to be persuasive about anything. If the witness knows something, we need to know it if it's relevant but if he's guessing it's not going to help fishing for him to guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You indicated that you went back to Velepromet where you saw Judge Vojnovic again. Do you recall what was going on at Velepromet at the time?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I met the Prime Minister, minister Hadzic, Dokmanovic, and the president of the Jagodina municipality there. All those who were members of the cabinet and whom I knew. I spent sometime with them. And as I had no other obligations, I attended the government meeting. In the meantime, I can't recall clearly whether I went to intercede on behalf of Mrs. Clearic's son. As I was on my way back to the health centre, near to the barracks, there was a convoy holding civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Now that you mention the meeting and the figures involved, we have a video clip that we would like to play before the Trial Chamber. Please watch it closely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have Exhibit 269 prepared from 6 minutes 20 seconds?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Let me just tell you this: Whenever you recognise anyone, if so, please say stop and tell us who that person is. The same applies to where you see yourself in that video clip.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Stop. Rade Leskovac and right at the outset Slavko Dokmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could we play the tape back a bit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. This is Slavko Dokmanovic, or so it seems. Stop. The one behind the back of this gentleman, wearing glasses is, I believe, Rade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Right. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. This is Vlado Kosic, the person wearing the uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: To the left of the other person?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Let us just record the minute. 6.44, for the benefit of the record. Can we play -- or rather, can you tell us who this person is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Rade Kosic, who was the manager of the water supplies company after the war. I'm not sure about what his position was before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. Goran Hadzic and Arkan. I believe this is Arkan, although the image is a bit blurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Let us just look at the minutes, at the time of the tape.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, here he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: 7.00. Right. Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Arkan is right alongside him. I don't know this man. Or this one. Stop. This is me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Explain to us which one of the two?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: The one in the background without the mustache.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Wearing a cap and the olive-grey uniform?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: For the record, this is at 7 minutes 18 seconds. Thank you. Let's carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. I believe that this is the president of the Jagodina municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: He was wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. Let us move back a bit. I believe that was Rade Stupar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Stupar?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Stupar, but what is his first name? Rade? I'm not sure. I'm certain about his family name. He was always alongside Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: 7.36 is the person you identified as Stupar. Let's carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was Arkan again, the same persons all over again. I find this person familiar but I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Let us wait a bit to see if someone else will come up. Can you tell us the building we see behind the people, was this where the meeting of the government was?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: To the left of what we saw on the scene, there was a conference hall there, with tables and chairs, and that was where the government sat. These are all civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I think this is enough. Thank you. Do you remember when you left Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I think this was before the session of the government. I went to see Mrksic and then I went back immediately by car.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: The distance from Velepromet to the place where Mrksic was is how many in kilometres?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Three to four kilometres away, maybe even less.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you recall anything else that happened specifically on that day at Velepromet or elsewhere or would that be all?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I can remember partially. I have only partial memory. I remember I attended this but not all the time. I don't remember all the participants at the meeting, all the members of the cabinet who were there. I remember later on seeing Mr. Sljivancanin, his deputy, like Vukasinovic, Palic, Panic, I think it was Panic. I don't remember his rank, mayor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say Panic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: He was deputy to Colonel Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us something about your career after these events in November 1991?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: You mean as a civilian?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, in general.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I resigned from all these functions, and I received a proposal to form, to establish a company. We had only four vehicles left that were damaged in the war. We had received some vehicles and we established a new company, and then they asked me to activate in the Republic of Srpska army, and I was the deputy commander of the logistics, and then I moved on to the command of the corps. I was deputy of the chief of security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the witness said -- I think I saw Sljivancanin, Vukasinovic and Panic. And this is not what it says in the transcript. I think if the witness cannot confirm this --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were two of them. I'm not sure about Panic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Wait, please. We can't have two people speaking. Nothing can be heard on the recording. If you would wait for a particular question. Now, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to note regarding the transcript on page 77 line 11, I think that the witness said, "I think I saw Sljivancanin, Vukasinovic and Panic." I would just like to verify if this is correct. I am not seeking for a confirmation by the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, would you deal with that matter, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'll try to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You mentioned three officers, Sljivancanin, Vukasinovic, Panic. Are you sure that you saw all three of them or do you have any doubts as to seeing some of them? Could you please clarify?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: The two of them were there. As for Panic, I'm not sure if he joined in later on. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 77, line 25, you said that you joined the Republic of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I think you said Krajina so I would like to have this correction entered in the transcript. You are talking about the army of the Republika Srpska Krajina. Could you please clarify -- I think you were speaking rather fast, for the sake of the transcript, when you took up this function which positions did you have?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Was the commander of the logistics base of the Srem and the Baranja corps. And since I have completed also a security military school, I then went on to the security command, assistant to the chief of security for the command chief affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does this mean that you were chief of security and your function was assistant?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say that you completed the army -- does this refer to the training?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. It refers to trainings that I undertook in Pancevo and in other places. There were many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: While performing this function, which rules did you abide by? Were there any specific rules or did the JNA rules apply?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: The JNA rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does this refer to the security organs as well?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. The entire training of commanding officers was done according to the JNA rules of service.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I suppose you're very familiar with these rules and the standard practice at the time?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember your specific functions as security officer in terms of issuing commands or in terms of liaising with the military police?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. I in fact was commanding the military police elements. I was issuing them orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Please continue. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I was issuing assignments to the commanders of certain squads when needed, so I had the authority to do this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Of course, with the approval of the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was this standard practice while you were still in the JNA or was it different?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object, Your Honour, at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This is well outside of the proofing notes. It's well outside of the 65 ter notes and the additional 65 ter notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet? Has there been notice given of these facts?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not regarding the last ones, because we finished the preparations of the witness very late last evening. Therefore, I do not insist on this point if there is objection on the part of the Prosecution, although I did not intend to pursue this line of questioning. I was about to finish this line of questioning and not only this line of questioning but my examination-in-chief of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Domazet. The evidence about that matter will not be taken into consideration. And thank you for your examination. Now Mr. Borovic, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have a few questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Hello, my name is Mr. Borovic, representing Mr. Radic here. In your rely to Mr. Domazet's question, you said that you used the terms, I sat the course. My question is as follows: Did you, in the area where you were located during the operations, in fact -- were you in a position to issue commands? Second question: To whom did you issue commands?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I had a direct connection with the commanders of the squads and the companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that the answer were you able to command because the witness replied that he was able to command over the commanders of the companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When you refer to commanders of the companies, which companies are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Four companies that were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When you are referring to the existing four companies, are you referring to the companies of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, Territorial Defence, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said today also that Colonel Mrksic ordered four members of Territorial Defence to be in front of the JNA units, to lead them.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, since they were familiar with the streets and the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please wait when giving your answer in order to avoid overlaps? Does this mean that this was the main reason for which the Territorial Defence units in fact joined in operations with the JNA, because they were familiar with the access, with the terrain, et cetera? Was this the main reason for this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: This was one of the reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you familiar with the sites of the shelters, atomic shelters, in the city of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the main one was in the yard on the courtyard of the Territorial Defence headquarters, next to the municipal building of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During the operations, who was controlling the headquarters of the staff, Territorial Defence Staff, in November 1991, where the atomic shelter was located?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you say Croats, you mean -- you are referring to paramilitary formations, also known as ZNG?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the existence of a shelter at Komerc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know there was a shelter for civilians there. I don't know if it was an atomic shelter or if it was merely a warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I told you that the defence has come about certain information that an atomic shelter was located there, my question would be the following: In the period from November, from October to November, under whose control was this shelter?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Under the control of the ZNG.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about Luzac? Was there an atomic shelter there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not familiar with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know of another shelter which was located in the MUP premises, in the --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: In the basement of the MUP building, there were detention facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In order to avoid speculation, could you please answer the following question: Was it under the control of the Territorial Defence or was there any shelter that was under the control of the Territorial Defence or the JNA in Vukovar before the liberation of Vukovar, of course?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: There was no shelter under the control of either JNA or the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So can we conclude that all the shelters during the operations were under the control of paramilitary formations and the Croatian MUP?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This goes back to the issue of co-counsel. Are they allowed to cross or must they use the examination-in-chief or direct questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Hence the position they are taking, Mr. Weiner, as I explained. I don't detect any conflict over this at the moment. You're off in an area not dealt with by Mr. Domazet, so if you could avoid cross-examination and go back to examining the witness. Thank you, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. There will be other witnesses for which I will request the Trial Chamber to allow me to cross-examine them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: From whom did you receive orders?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: From Mr. Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell the Trial Chamber where the main operations staff was located for liberating Vukovar? Where exactly was that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: The main operations staff for the liberation of Vukovar, if you're talking about OG South, that was based in Negoslavci. It's a village near Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who the staff comprised?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I don't know all of them. I've forgotten some over time, but I know that all the usual commanding officers were there, all the branches and all the arms and all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you ever heard of Major Borivoj Tesic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who is he?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 1st mixed Battalion or the 1st Battalion of the Guards Brigade. We were personally together at the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Where was his own headquarters, his own command post?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: His command post was at Svetozara Markovica street in Jagatic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who was at the command post when you were having talks and planning military operations?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Myself, Mr. Tesic and Mr. Stijakovic, his deputy, as well as my own deputy, Milanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Were you ever there when his company commanders, company commanders of the 1st Motorised Battalion came to briefings and to be debriefed or to take orders from Borivoj Tesic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: For the most part, I was the one receiving company commanders at the time. I was with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of captain Sasa Bojkovski?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: He was the commander of the 3rd Company,.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Of the 1st Motorised Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it was called at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was a commander of a JNA company of the army?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: This company, did it belong to the 1st motorised Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that he was the commander of the 3rd Company of the 1st Motorised Battalion, establishment-wise?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, page 85, line 12. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Line 12, the names are wrong. There is one missing, I think the name missing is Ivanovic, but I think Mr. Borovic might perhaps want to -- clearly, you see there is no such names and all the others I can't see them, there were three names, so I think that therefore this should be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic [Microphone not activated] I think the speed and difficulty of picking up precise pronunciations has led to a group of names there that require some revisiting. Would you be able to do that and --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the 1st Motorised Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Major Borivoj Tesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about his deputy?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Captain Stijakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The command post of the 1st Motorised Battalion, Colonel Tesic was in charge; right? When you received your assignments there, who was present? Slowly, please. Which persons?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Whether we received our assignments?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When Borivoj Tesic handed out your assignments, who was present?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: The company commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And Stijakovic and yourself?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: I was also handing out assignments to company commanders and so was he. If there was anything extraordinary that needed tackling.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Were you ever positioned along the axis of operations of Sasa Bojkovski's company?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Which axis was that, if you would be so kind, please?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: It was Pionirsko Naselje. And that street, I've forgotten all the street names in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if there was a creche or a kindergarten somewhere along that axis?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The Petrova Gora TO detachment in November, how strong were they? How many men? Which level in the military sense?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: The level of a battalion, should have been. It's an independent unit, this detachment. The level of a battalion that can act independently, a battalion is part of a brigade and a detachment is an independent unit and that is precisely why it is called a detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that your detachment could not be incorporated into any of the battalions' companies?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: If necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: No, I mean is it possible --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please wait?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Once again, that's a very leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Borovic. You better try again a different way, if you would.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Establishment-wise, can a detachment be subordinated to a company that is part of a battalion? Can it be absorbed by this company, establishment-wise?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Depends on the level of equipment the company owns, how trained they are on the level of training of their commander. It's possible. As a matter of principle, this is not the done thing, but that doesn't mean it's not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Establishment-wise, how strong is a detachment normally?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: That depends. That depends.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the speakers kindly be asked to speak one at the same time, otherwise we can't hear them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
