utterances.text: You need to talk slowly, you need to talk slowly. We are hardly getting anything on to the transcript, establishment-wise, the Petrova Gora detachment, how strong was it, how many men?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You've completed a reserve officers school. Did you perhaps learn there, establishment-wise, how strong a JNA company normally is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: A company has about three platoons which amounts to about 120 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If you have a company which can have up to 120 men, establishment-wise, how do you fit a 400-strong detachment into that sort of thing, in terms of establishment?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Has this been known to happen?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Not really. Just purely in theory, establishment-wise. If you say it's not possible, we'll rest at that.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: That depends on the situation, that depends on the purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I won't be pressing you on this. I won't keep confusing you on this, I won't be leading you any more. It's not that important, really. What was the axis of operations for Zirovic's company, captain Zirovic's company?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: That was at Svetozara Markovica street. The left-hand side of the street. Across the way from Kruno the butcher's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Have you provided any statements to The Hague investigators? I mean the investigators of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: They came to see me at home about the Dokmanovic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And you gave a statement, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was still in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You signed this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, or at least I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The use of TO members and volunteers in Vukovar, who was the only person in charge of this? Who was the top man who could have determined what the needs were, along what axis and how they should work together with JNA units? Whose call was this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: The commander of the operations group.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The name being?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JAKSIC
utterances.text: Mile Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Borovic. Now, Mr. Lukic, four minutes. You're going to leave it to Mr. Bulatovic. Is four minutes of use to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, Your Honours, I don't think four minutes will do, because of the serious nature of this evidence we need more time to cross-examine him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I was giving you an opportunity, if you wanted, the four minutes. Otherwise, I'm thinking that you would like to start tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I don't think there is any point in starting now and then breaking in a couple of minutes. So unless the Chamber minds, I think it might be a good idea to resume tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, very briefly I would like to apologise to the Court for being late at the beginning of the second session. I assure the Court it will not occur again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I was going to leave this for tomorrow, but I still have two minutes, so that's not a problem. Unfortunately my news is not good and that is the reason I have decided to address you. Our first piece of news is that Defence witness Puskar who was supposed to be arriving in The Hague today, unfortunately, suffered a heart attack two days ago, a stroke, and he has been hospitalised and is still in hospital receiving treatment. We hope that he will be fine eventually and the Defence will be filing a further motion with the Trial Chamber to maybe hear this witness towards the end of our Defence case, if that is possible. Secondly, this is about that protected witness. I'm trying to avoid private session now. We all know what I'm talking about. We only received the appropriate medical document in relation to this witness today, so we will have a look and at first glance what I can say is that the documents indicate that the witness could not start testifying on the 16th, as had originally been planned. But we'll have a closer look at these documents and files today to see what exactly the documents say. The good news is we got the passport for that witness who had not had his passport issued. So the good bit is that all our witnesses now have passports. We are expecting Lisanovic here and if our cooperation remains good with the Victims and Witnesses Unit -- I have to praise them a little because the last time around, it seemed as if I had been scolding them. I hope the witness makes it. Plus another witness, who has received his call-up, I hope he'll be appearing towards the end of next week. As well as the witness who is due back on the 20th of September, who is now away but should be back, I think an approval has already been granted, the passport is there, and of course the expert, and that's all our witnesses, Your Honours. I have tried to give you a briefer overview of our witness situation as it now stands on behalf of Mr. Mrksic. I really hope that we can wrap this up successfully and very soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, can you just make clearer for me your position tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is the situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If this witness concludes tomorrow, although I do believe that my learned friends will have a lot of questions for this witness, we still have another witness in the wings, as it were, Mr. Milosevic, who arrived yesterday. So he could easily appear just after this witness. I do think, however, Mr. Milosevic is more likely to be appearing on Monday. I think we will need the whole of tomorrow for this witness, given the nature of all the topics that have been raised. He might take all day, the way it seems. We do have Mr. Milosevic on standby and he can certainly jump in if needed. I sincerely hope that we can have Mr. Lisanovic over here this coming weekend and perhaps he could or not. He could testify on the 20th. No. The news is not as good as I was hoping unfortunately. My assistant just told me that Lisanovic could appear on the 20th. Although --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: At the moment it would appear then that you will be getting into some embarrassment early next week; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what it looks like for the time being, Your Honours. I'm certainly hoping for improvements in this situation, if Mr. Lisanovic makes it here on Sunday, he could easily start on Monday or on Tuesday. I think his testimony will take up two days. That is my prediction. In that case, we would cover all the time until the return of Witness Dannilovic. Some confusion was caused by the belief that the protected witness would be appearing on the 16th and that he would thus cover three days of our case. As I have already indicated, he has now sent us some documents, we will be looking at that, but that may cause a problem. Documents permitting, we might be filing a motion with the Trial Chamber to perhaps have this witness testify via videolink, if indeed it turns out to be a problem for him to travel given his condition. But we only received these documents earlier today and for the time being I can't say anything more than I have already indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Vasic, if you would give some very close attention to the arrival and readiness of your witnesses and ensure other counsel know, all three other sets of counsel know, who is coming, in what order so it becomes clear so that they can prepare. And if you could be very careful in your examination of these witnesses so that we don't just use up time that you may well very greatly need if for some reason there is a delay in witnesses arriving here. We want to be sure there is adequate time to hear the evidence that is important from them. Don't just waste time with some other witnesses on matters that aren't critical. We will see what tomorrow holds. We adjourn now until 9.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: be reconvened on Friday, the 15th day of September, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.50 p.m., to
